headline: Elon Musk wants his Terafab chip project to test ten chip design versions a year, but a digitimes analysis points to cost and equipment hurdles.
score_reason: Lowered by 1 from 5: the event was on 11 Oct 2026 and the item is an analysis of a plan with no timeline.
importance_line: It matters to chipmakers and Tesla and SpaceX investors, and it describes a goal with no timeline, not a working factory.
summary: digitimes reports in an analysis that Tesla chief executive Elon Musk said at a Tesla event in Austin on 11 Oct 2026 "I don't know how to make chips" but "We'll figure it out", setting a target of 10 chip design iterations a year for the Terafab project, against about one generation every two years across the industry. The analysis says photomask costs for 3nm chips can reach US$5 million to US$20 million per set, Musk gave no timeline beyond saying it could take several years, and Intel's and Tesla's continued participation is still subject to later agreements.
